Traditional finance is undergoing a structural reset as markets brace for the upcoming FOMC meeting on June 16–17, the first chaired by the newly sworn-in Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. Persistent inflation, coupled with May’s resilient non-farm payrolls of 172,000, has dashed expectations for near-term rate cuts. Consequently, US 10-year Treasury yields have surged to 4.92%, dampening risk sentiment and triggering equities sell-offs.

This macroeconomic pressure transmits directly to digital assets. Bitcoin corrected from $72,000 to $64,000, exacerbated by record-breaking US spot ETF outflows of $3.15 billion over eleven days. Meanwhile, the launch of Nasdaq CME Crypto Index futures on June 8 represents a major regulatory milestone, creating regulated hedging tools for institutions.

Ultimately, these developments highlight an intensifying correlation between traditional and crypto markets. High sovereign yields drain risk-on liquidity from both equities and digital assets, while incoming European EMT frameworks and US index futures solidify crypto as a regulated extension of the traditional financial system. Consequently, crypto is no longer an isolated hedge; instead, it moves in tandem with macro liquidity cycles, where regulatory integrations act as transmission lines that convert traditional monetary policy directly into digital asset volatility.
